checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add score time-stretch

impact_assessment.why: Changing the tempo of a score by scaling its event timeline is a basic editing operation distinct from the global tempo override.
impact_assessment.benefits: stretch scales every start and duration by a factor, preserving pitch and timbre, with factor 1 as an exact identity.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: factor must be positive and finite, all non-timing fields must be preserved, and output must re-serialize exactly; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure stretch module with identity, scaling and preservation tests, a CLI command, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 178 tests green; stretch identity, scaling and field preservation pinned by byte tests
Task 'coda-stretch' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add RMS-targeted normalization

impact_assessment.why: Peak normalization can leave a quiet-sounding track at full peak; loudness work needs an RMS target mode.
impact_assessment.benefits: normalize --rms-target <dBFS> scales a Coda WAV to a chosen RMS level with deterministic clamping, complementing peak mode.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: silence must be left unchanged, invalid dBFS targets must fail clearly, and peak mode must stay byte-identical; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure RMS gain function with known-vector and silence tests, extend the normalize CLI, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 179 tests green; RMS target verified by analyze, peak mode unchanged
Task 'coda-rms-normalize' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add crossfaded section joining

impact_assessment.why: join currently hard-cuts between sections, which clicks; an equal-power crossfade makes assembled pieces continuous.
impact_assessment.benefits: join --crossfade S overlaps adjacent sections with a deterministic fade, producing a continuous WAV whose length accounts for the overlap.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: crossfade 0 must stay byte-identical to current join, overlaps must clamp to the shorter section, and output length must shrink by the overlap; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure crossfade join function with length and blend byte tests, extend the CLI option, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 182 tests green; crossfade blend, clamping, shorter length and zero-overlap identity pinned by byte tests
Task 'coda-crossfade' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: 0b1ffcae13d2d326216045c79c59d0be73321c4d

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add WAV time and silence trimming

impact_assessment.why: Rendered WAVs often have leading or trailing silence, or need an excerpt; there is no Coda tool to cut audio without an external editor.
impact_assessment.benefits: trim selects an exact time range or auto-detects non-silent content with a threshold, writing a valid Coda WAV.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: invalid ranges must fail clearly, an all-silent file must stay valid, and no-op trims must be byte-identical; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure trim module with exact frame-range and silence-detection byte tests, a CLI command, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 188 tests green; time-range and silence trimming verified by byte length and analyze
Task 'coda-trim' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add named fade presets for WAV files

impact_assessment.why: Fades currently require knowing exact seconds at render time; applying named fades to an existing WAV is a common finishing step.
impact_assessment.benefits: fade --preset applies short/gentle/long/tail/attack envelopes to any Coda WAV using the existing deterministic fade code.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: presets must be bounded by half the buffer, unknown names must fail clearly, and output must stay a valid WAV; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a preset lookup with exact edge-frame tests, a CLI command, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 193 tests green; fade preset names, edge attenuation and unchanged length pinned by byte tests
Task 'coda-fade-presets' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add score looping to canonical source

impact_assessment.why: Repeating a phrase is a basic arrangement operation; producing it as editable source is better than only concatenating rendered audio.
impact_assessment.benefits: loop repeats all notes N times with correct time offsets, writing canonical source that round-trips and composes with the other transforms.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: times 1 must be byte-identical, offsets must use the score's full duration, and invalid counts must fail clearly; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure loop module with identity, offset and preservation byte tests, a CLI command, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 198 tests green; loop identity, offsets and doubled duration pinned by byte tests
Task 'coda-loop' completed successfully.
